q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) NUM FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING NUM >= 5 ) AS A
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) NUM FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING NUM >= 5 ) AS A
explanation: Q1 groups by CLASS and checks if the count of rows (i.e., students) in each class is >= 5. Q2 groups by CLASS, counts the distinct students in each class, and checks if this count is >= 5. The difference lies in the COUNT function used: Q1 uses COUNT(*), which counts all rows, while Q2 uses COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT), which counts unique students.
counterexample_dsp: A class with 5 students where 2 students are enrolled in other classes as well. Q1 will count this class as it has 5 rows, while Q2 will not count it as it has only 3 unique students.
